name: Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining
description: This is a collection of 23 industrial sites, mostly in southwest Japan, including ironworks, shipyards and coal mines. They show how Japan, between the 1850s and 1910, absorbed Western technology and reshaped it to suit its own needs. It is widely seen as the first successful transfer of Western-style industrialization to a non-Western country, and it changed the nation within a few decades.
